correctness.rationale: TARGET side-A proof is not rigorous. Step 2 rho identity (2) is false as stated: Livsic coboundary gives rho_f = rho_g*(P(x)/P(y)), not equality; telescoping argument omits surviving -u(y)+u(x) term and confuses coboundary rho with matching. Step 1 leafwise C-infinity bootstrap is circular because phi|Ws = a_f^s - a_g^s o h is only Holder (h only Holder a priori), so phi is not C^r along contracting foliation. Step 3 conformal bootstrap is hand-waving: no proof that h|Wu is quasiregular/ACL with bounded dilatation, no Beltrami estimate from (3), single matching function insufficient for inverse-function-theorem, Weyl/Ahlfors-Bers invoked without Sobolev regularity. Step 4 Journe hypotheses (uniform C^r along both foliations) never established. Artifacts verify only linear-model telescoping and O(|u||s|) quad bound, not nonlinear rigidity.

originality.rationale: Headline claims unconditional stable-Jacobian-only C-infinity rigidity for complex T^3 pair with no very-non-algebraic and no SRB!=MME exception. Nearest prior Gogolev-Rodriguez Hertz arXiv:2105.10539 proves only conditional version: matching Jacobian => smooth OR SRB=MME, and Corollary 1.3 for stable-only with same alternative plus very-non-algebraic open-dense hypothesis. Kalinin-Sadovskaya/Gogolev require full periodic data or real-spectrum bootstrap. No prior states or implies the unconditional stable-only claim; it is strictly stronger than GRH and not a recomputation, table lookup, or synonymous restatement. Hence statement-novelty passes though proof fails.

value.rationale: TARGET dichotomy is motivated before computation: whether 1D stable periodic data alone forces smooth conjugacy for C1-close complex T^3 Anosov pair, with sharp complex-vs-real boundary and Livsic/matching-function attack. An unconditional rigidity theorem would advance recognized Anosov rigidity program beyond GRH conditional result and clarify sharpness. This is a new theorem form, not textbook restatement, parameter substitution, tiny gain, or unexplained enumeration. Value holds independently of proof defect.
